HELPING GIRLS' AMBITIONS TAKE OFF
The launchpad for your daughter's future success
An independent, private school in Hampshire, England for girls 3 to 18 years. Here girls learn without limits in an environment designed for discovery and achieving ambitions.
Welcome
It gives me enormous pleasure to welcome you to Portsmouth High School. A school where you can be sure your daughter will thrive. Because we are resolute in our ambition to make sure that whoever she is, and whoever she wants to become, we will be there – every step of the way – to help her fulfil her promise, and her ambitions.
Sarah Parker MA (Hons) Head, Portsmouth High School GDST
Who we are
Portsmouth High School is part of the Girls’ Day School Trust, the leading network of independent girls’ schools in the UK. The GDST is a family of twenty-four independent schools and two academies across the country, dedicated to academic and pastoral excellence.
As pioneers and shapers of girls’ education for 153 years, we put girls first, tailoring their learning experiences to nurture confident, happy and fearless young women. Our forward-thinking approach to education provides development opportunities beyond the curriculum and equips girls with the skills and attributes to become the leaders and changemakers of the future on their own terms.
Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) Report 2026
Portsmouth High School GDST is delighted to share that our recent ISI inspection found that the school met all Standards. Inspectors praised our strong pastoral care, inclusive ethos and ‘culture of care and mutual respect.’
The curriculum was highlighted as well planned and ambitious, with excellent literacy provision. Older pupils achieve well, and those with special educational needs receive effective support. Early Years staff were praised for inspiring a love of learning.
Our wide co‑curricular programme, pupils’ strong values, and high‑quality careers guidance were also commended.
Safeguarding was judged ‘thorough and robust.’
Book a Family Tour
Portsmouth High School is open for bespoke family tours throughout the year whether your daughter is looking to join the nursery, pre-school, prep school, senior school or sixth form. Visit our Family Tour page to find out more.
Request a Prospectus
As part of Portsmouth High School’s commitment to supporting the environment we no longer print prospectuses. You can download the latest copy of our pre-school, prep school, senior school and sixth form prospectuses from our website.

Portsmouth High School, GDST, senior awards; ‘…if you don’t like the world you’re in, have the courage to go and change it’
Portsmouth High School’s senior students were the proud recipients of achievement awards, certificates and cups this week as friends, family, pupils and staff from the school gathered for an evening of celebration. The guest speaker was an alumna of Portsmouth High School, Annalee Macfarlane (Class of 2022) who has been, since leaving Portsmouth High School, on an Apprenticeship Degree at Rolls-Royce, most recently a Power Verification Strategy Lead.
Last year’s leavers returned to school to receive their awards before starting at universities later this month. Courses they are taking range from Politics and International Relations, Geography and Finance to Psychology, Environmental Geoscience, Paramedic Science and Multimedia Sports Journalism.
Attended by The Deputy Lord Mayor of Portsmouth, Councillor Suzy Horton and her Deputy Lady Mayoress, Jo McDougall (both Portsmouth High School alumnae), The Mayor of Fareham, Councillor Tina Ellis and Consort, Councillor Robert Ellis, The Deputy Mayor and Deputy Mayoress of Gosport, Councillor Kevin Casey and Mrs Hazel Casey, Chair of Governors, Commodore Chris Plamer, former Chair of Governors, Mrs Krysia Butwilowska, Editor in Chief of the Portsmouth News, Mr Mark Waldren and other distinguished guests, staff, parents and pupils.
Achievements were celebrated across the older year groups and pupils received awards from sports and drama colours to Duke of Edinburgh Awards, music cups, social responsibility prizes and academic year prizes.
Headmistress, Mrs Sarah Parker, introduced the evening:
‘While academic achievements deserve celebration, they tell only part of the story. The true measure of a school’s success lies in the character of the young people who leave it. We hope our pupils leave not only as accomplished learners but also as thoughtful, compassionate, resilient and courageous young women, equipped to make a positive contribution wherever life takes them.’
Deputy Head Girl, Farah, introduced the guest speaker, Annalee Macfarlane, who said:
‘If I pause and consider my route into aerospace engineering and what has brought me to stand before you today, I am grateful that I never once had to ask the question ‘is engineering the right career for me as a woman?’ At no point throughout my education – or indeed my career – has my gender felt like a barrier, quite the opposite in fact… …far more important than what subjects you choose to study or what university of what job you pursue is to ask the question, “what sort of person do I want to be.”’
Annalee talked about her apprenticeship degree but has recently decided to make a significant career change. She is starting work with Shelter, the national campaign to end homelessness, whilst also undertaking a part-time Masters in International Humanitarian Affairs.
The evening heard speeches from pupils including Alice about the sports tour to Dubai, Sherri on the Krakow trip and Cerys talked about the GDST LEAD business scheme. Music was played by students, Emma, Evelyn and Lauren. Lauren played her own composition ‘Lines’ which won the Never Such Innocence global competition. Never Such Innocence is a charity dedicated to amplifying the voices of young people and children affected by war and conflict. Lauren drew inspiration from a history lesson exploring the impact of the Berlin Wall. Reflecting on the division of families, friends and an entire city, she questioned how such separation could affect so many lives. These ideas formed the emotional core of her song, which examines the human cost of conflict and division.
Lauren also received the Alisha Zaman Memorial Sixth Form Talent Scholarship. This award has been established by annual donations from the family of the late Alisha Jenni Zaman, a student at Portsmouth High School 2004-2017 in loving memory of her time and growing up as a student from Year 1 to Year 13. This scholarship is inspired by Alisha’s wish to give something back to her school where she passed her childhood and early adulthood.
The guest speaker, Annalee, added:
‘It’s okay to not know what you want to do with your life. But whatever you do, bring your 100%. And if you don’t like the world you’re in, have the courage to go and change it.’
Deputy Lord Mayor of Portsmouth concluded:
‘It was back to school (literally!) for Jo, my Deputy Lady Mayoress, and I to attend the Senior Awards evening.
‘Many things have changed since we met at PHS nearly 50 years ago; for example the buildings and a much broader curriculum emphasising the arts and sport. All improvements in our opinion.
‘But some things stay the same; the emphasis on friendships, academic achievement, ambition and what impact a PHS girl can make on improving the world by becoming the best version of herself.
‘As the years roll by, we feel that more than ever.’

Portsmouth High School, GDST, celebrates successes for Years 7-9
Pupils at Portsmouth High School, GDST, were proud recipients of awards at an evening of celebration this week.
Head, Mrs Sarah Parker, presented the prizes, with music interludes from Grace on cello, Olivia, voice and Saffy on piano.
Pupils, Florence, Jessica, Charlotte and Izzy, gave the audience a small taste of the range of opportunities they have experienced throughout the year, including raising funds for Canine Partners, partaking in Duke of Edinburgh Awards and Bushcraft Camp.
‘One of the biggest highlights was our ISI inspection,’ said Mrs Parker. ‘An inspection can feel daunting, but it also gave us the opportunity to show inspectors what we already know—that this is a school where girls are encouraged to aim high, to support one another and to become confident, compassionate young people.
‘To our award winners this evening,’ she continued, ‘Congratulations. Awards are a wonderful way of recognising achievement, but they don’t tell the whole story. Some of your greatest achievements won’t be written on a certificate. They will be the times you kept going when something was difficult, the moments you showed kindness to someone who needed it, the confidence you found to try something new, or the friendships you have built along the way.
‘Thank you to our parents and families for your continued encouragement and support, and thank you to all of our staff for the dedication and care you show our pupils every day.’

Portsmouth High School, GDST, celebrates creativity and innovation at annual Art and Design Technology Exhibition
Portsmouth High School, GDST, celebrated the creativity, talent and hard work of its students through this year’s Art and Design Technology Exhibition, which featured an inspiring collection of work developed over the previous two years.
The exhibition brought together a diverse range of projects, highlighting the many ways students had explored ideas, materials and processes to create highly individual outcomes. From imaginative artistic responses to innovative design solutions, each piece reflected a unique creative journey and demonstrated the breadth of talent across the school.
Visitors were able to view not only the finished pieces but also the development process behind them, gaining an insight into the research, experimentation and problem-solving that had shaped each project.
Mrs Emma Noble, Head of the Faculty of Creative Arts at Portsmouth High School, said:
‘This year’s Art and Design Technology Exhibition was a celebration of creativity, innovation and individual expression, showcasing the talent, dedication and hard work of our students.
‘Through a diverse range of approaches, materials and ideas, the exhibition highlighted how creativity can take many forms, with each piece reflecting a unique perspective and design journey.’
Throughout the previous two years, students had demonstrated resilience, commitment and a willingness to take creative risks as they refined their ideas and developed their final outcomes.
‘The exhibition was an important opportunity to recognise and celebrate the commitment, resilience and imagination that students invested in their work throughout the last two years,’ said Mrs Noble.
‘From initial concepts to finished outcomes, every project demonstrated not only technical skill but also the confidence to experiment, problem-solve and communicate ideas in meaningful ways.’
The exhibition also highlighted the vital role creativity plays in education and society, encouraging students to explore different perspectives and communicate their ideas with confidence.
Mrs Noble added: ‘Creativity is an essential part of culture. It helps us make sense of the world, share ideas and tell stories that connect people and communities. The work on display reflected this spirit, and we were proud to celebrate the achievements of our students and the originality, thought and care they brought to their projects.’
The exhibition was a testament to the imagination, skill and determination of Portsmouth High School students, celebrating not only their artistic and technical achievements but also the creative thinking that will support them in their future studies and careers.

Almost half of all grades A*/9 for Portsmouth High School, GDST
Pupils at Portsmouth High School GDST were celebrating this morning after receiving their GCSE results; with almost half of all grades A*/9 and 94% grades A*-B equivalent.
‘We are delighted, once again, to celebrate an exceptional set of GCSE results achieved by our pupils,’ said Head, Mrs Sarah Parker. ‘These successes are a testament to their commitment and perseverance, the outstanding support of our teaching staff, and the culture of ambition and hard work that is embedded throughout the school. They also reflect the confidence, leadership and academic excellence that can flourish in a girls-only educational environment, where every pupil is encouraged to fulfil her potential without limits.’
Twins, Hettie and Molly, gained 20 top grades between them – with 11 x 9s, 4 x A*s, 2 8s and 3 x 7s.
‘There was lots of dedication to revision,’ said Molly. ‘Support from friends and studying together to try and make it fun, was definitely a factor in getting today’s results. That, and lots of snacks,’ she added. ‘I’m really excited about coming back for Sixth Form. All the teachers know me and I’m looking forward to studying for A Levels in Biology, Chemistry and Religious Studies.’
Twin sister, Hettie, will also be studying for A Levels alongside her sister in Biology and Chemistry and will add in Politics instead of RS. ‘We mainly revised together,’ she said. ‘But lots of revision with friends too and we have had amazing support from teachers.’
Isabella, gained 8 x 9 grades and 2 x A*s and was thrilled with her results.
‘I will be coming back in September and really hope to become a doctor one day,’ she said. ‘I am just so pleased and excited.’
Chloe, was equally delighted with her grades of A*s, 9s and 8s.
‘I’m so excited. Definitely off to celebrate now,’ she said. ‘I’ll be back in September and really excited about joining the Sixth Form.’
Lauren, who received A*s, As and 9s will be returning to take Music as one of her three A Levels in September. She wants to pursue a career in music after earning international recognition for winning a top prize in a global competition run by the charity ‘Never Such Innocence.’
‘I have had so much support from my friends, my family and my teachers,’ she said.
‘This is a truly remarkable year group, and I am absolutely delighted for them,’ said Mrs Julie Parkinson, Head of Year 11. ‘Their results are a testament to the hard work, determination and positive attitude they have shown throughout their GCSE studies. It has been a privilege to see them grow and succeed, and it is wonderful to celebrate their achievements today. As they take their next steps, we are excited to welcome them back into Sixth Form, where we know they will continue to thrive and make the most of the opportunities ahead.’
Portsmouth High School, GDST, Open Morning is on Saturday 26 September from 10am-12noon.

THE SENIOR SCHOOL DIFFERENCE
Welcome to Portsmouth High School
These are some of the most important years of your daughter’s young life. Her experiences so far have ignited her imagination, built her confidence and helped her develop a strong sense of self. Our role, as senior school educators, is to nurture the person she is now and provide the scaffolding on which to build her dreams, so that she can grow into the future she envisions for herself.
We are proud of our girls...
We are proud of our academic track record (see our examination results), and we are especially proud of our girls for consistently achieving at this level. We watch in awe as they grow into happy, accomplished and talented young people. For them, success is more than academic excellence; it is the ability to face challenges and cope with all that growing up brings. It is about being human and doing the right thing by others. It is about being open, honest and accountable, filled with confidence, energy, courage and integrity.
Getting ready to fly...
Our girls are leaders who work well with others. They are serious about their goals, yet bring humour and joy to everyday life. They are preparing for lift-off.
As the team that supports them, we are there at every step of their journey. Our wellbeing centre, Daffodil House, brings together form tutors and heads of year with our welfare, counselling, psychology and pastoral staff to create a rock-solid emotional foundation. By the time they enter sixth form, they have developed their own style, are fully prepared for life beyond school, and are ready to fly.
The quality of pupils' academic achievements is excellent.

A Levels – 100% pass rate – 79% grades A*-B at Portsmouth High School, GDST
It has been another outstanding year for Portsmouth High School students as they opened their A Level results this morning. The school had 100% pass rate with 79% of the grades A*-B.
‘It has been another exciting morning at Portsmouth High School with a wonderful set of results,’ said Headmistress Mrs Sarah Parker. ‘We are immensely proud of our students and all they have achieved. These excellent A Level results are a testament to their hard work, determination and ambition. They also reflect the unique strengths of an all-girls education, where young women are encouraged to be confident, intellectually curious and unafraid to pursue their aspirations. We congratulate every student on their success and wish them every happiness as they take their next steps.’
Head Girl, Emma, 18, was thrilled with her results which will take her to Exeter to read Law. ‘Lots of locking in and revision – particularly after mocks – has led to the results today,’ she said.
Erin, 18, who is going to Manchester to read Politics, Philosophy and Economics added, ‘I think this school has helped cultivate how I’ve learned to revise and how best to study. The school has given me so much support along the way.’
Jasmine, 18, is taking an exciting route for her next steps. ‘I’m going to Solent University to do an Apprenticeship Degree in Nautical Science. I’ve wanted to do this since I was about 15. I will be training to be Third Officer on board merchant navy ships and yesterday I went to my company’s [Conway Merchant Navy and Watermark’s] new simulator, training in navigation and steering and received my brand new uniform.’
Katie, 17, has overcome severe medical set backs to gain her place at Loughborough to read Marketing. ‘I’ve been diabetic since I was 9 years old and suffered liver disease since Year 10 which briefly impacted GCSEs. In December of this year I was diagnosed with a bowel disease which meant a lot of time out of school, especially in the run up to A Levels. I was hospitalised in March and missed a month of school, right before the exams, which wasn’t ideal. But, everything has worked out and I couldn’t have asked for much more today.’
Head of Sixth Form, Mrs Katie Wood, added:
‘These outstanding results are a tribute to the dedication and ambition of our students. As an all-girls sixth form, we are proud to offer a community where young women champion one another’s success, challenge themselves academically and develop the confidence to pursue their aspirations without limits. It has been a privilege to watch this year group grow into accomplished, compassionate and determined young women, and we look forward to seeing all they achieve next.’
Portsmouth High School’s next Open Morning is on Saturday 26 September from 10am – 12 noon.

Two Oxbridge Graduates Lead Portsmouth High School GDST into the New Academic Year
As Portsmouth High School GDST looks ahead to the 2026/27 academic year, the school is proud to be led by two distinguished Oxbridge graduates whose shared passion for girls’ education, academic excellence and student wellbeing continues to shape the school’s success.
Head, Mrs Sarah Parker, an English graduate of the University of Oxford, and Head of Prep Mrs Ruth Irvine-Capel, who studied History at the University of Cambridge, bring exceptional experience, inspiring leadership and a deep commitment to helping every girl flourish.
A fierce advocate for girls’ education, Mrs Parker joined Portsmouth High School as Deputy Head in 2020 from Harrogate Ladies’ College, where she spent eight years as Head of English before becoming Deputy Head. She has also served as a Head of Sixth Form and has dedicated her career to ensuring girls are empowered to achieve their ambitions. Mrs Parker became Head of Portsmouth High School in 2024.
Having studied English at Oxford before completing her PGCE at Durham University, Mrs Parker understands first-hand the transformational power of education and the importance of encouraging young women to aim high.
‘It is a real privilege to begin a new academic year at Portsmouth High School,’ she said. ‘We are hugely excited about the opportunities ahead and about working together to ensure that every girl is known, valued and encouraged to make the very most of her potential.’
Alongside Mrs Parker, Portsmouth High Prep School is led by Ruth Irvine-Capel, who is already a familiar and much-loved member of the school community. Previously Assistant Head (Pastoral), she has spent the last five years helping to shape the Prep School’s academic and pastoral provision and is well known for her commitment to supporting every pupil’s individual journey.
A Girls’ Day School Trust (GDST) alumna herself, having attended Oxford High School, Mrs Irvine-Capel went on to read History at the University of Cambridge before completing her PGCE. Her career has included teaching and leadership positions in both state and independent schools, as well as experience as an advisory teacher.
As both an educator and parent, she believes passionately in the GDST’s mission to put girls first.
‘I have seen first-hand, not only as a teacher but also as a parent of daughters, the remarkable difference that the GDST ethos makes,’ she said. ‘I believe deeply that pastoral care and academic achievement go hand in hand. When girls feel safe, supported and valued, they are empowered to achieve their best. And when academic ambition is matched with excellent care, wellbeing and confidence soar.’
Reflecting on her role leading the Prep School, she added:
‘After five very happy years at Portsmouth High, I feel both privileged and excited to be taking over the reins as Head at the Prep School and working alongside Sarah Parker and our wonderful staff in delivering our tailor-made academic and pastoral offer for girls in our local area.’
Together, Mrs Parker and Mrs Irvine-Capel embody the values at the heart of Portsmouth High School GDST: intellectual curiosity, ambition, compassion and confidence. As graduates of Oxford and Cambridge, they serve as inspiring role models for pupils, demonstrating the power of academic aspiration while championing an education that nurtures the whole child.
As the school community embarks on a new academic year, their combined leadership will continue to ensure that every girl is challenged academically, supported pastorally and empowered to become the very best version of herself.

Back to School: Alumnae Reunite Across Seven Decades
Up to seventy years after leaving Portsmouth High School, alumnae from the Classes of 1956, 1966, 1976, 1986, 1996, 2006 and 2016 returned to school last weekend for a special reunion lunch and tours of both the Senior and Prep Schools.
Led by current sixth form students, the tours sparked countless memories, with visitors sharing stories of school life, comparing past and present, and often pausing for laughter and reminiscence along the way.
Isobel, Year 13, was one of the sixth form students hosting the tours. She said:
‘It was a real privilege to show our alumnae around the school and share how it has grown while still keeping the same sense of community. Hearing their memories made me realise just how strong the Portsmouth High School family is, no matter what generation you belong to.’
Among those returning was Mrs Pamela Snow (née Sorrell), from the Class of 1956, who reflected on her visit:
‘It was such fun to see the many changes and still to recall our days at PHS. In reality many, many years ago, but still easily recalled. There are so very many more opportunities open to the young of today, but so many more challenges; it does seem the staff members are meeting those with sympathy and common sense.’
Mrs Helen Wynne-Griffith (née Sandover), from the Class of 1966, added:
‘Sixty years on, the buildings might not be quite the same, but the “Happy Vibes” of our memories were everywhere. Smiling faces and laughter showed what an important part of our lives, PHS had been.’
The reunion also provided an opportunity to celebrate the official opening of The Prescott Hall, the school’s newly refurbished dining hall, named in honour of former Headmistress Mrs Jane Prescott.
Addressing the gathered alumnae, Head, Mrs Sarah Parker, said:
‘It is a joy to welcome our alumnae back to the school that helped shape your journeys and to celebrate the enduring bonds of our community.
‘Thank you to Mrs Prescott for returning to Portsmouth High School to officially open the new Dining Hall which has been refurbished in her name; The Prescott Hall.’
Former Headmistress Mrs Jane Prescott, who led the school from 2011 to 2024, added:
‘I was honoured to return to Portsmouth High School to see the amazing refurbishment of the new Prescott Hall. It was wonderful to chat to the alumnae from the Class of 1956 right up to the Class of 2016 and all those in between. PHS is a very special place.’
The event highlighted the lifelong connection alumnae share with Portsmouth High School, bringing together former pupils spanning seven decades and demonstrating the enduring strength of the school community.

The Nursery and Pre-School Difference
Welcome
It is my great pleasure to welcome you to our Early Years provision, a warm and inclusive setting where we always put children’s wellbeing at the heart of all that we do, whilst giving them every opportunity to grow and thrive in all aspects of their development.
At Portsmouth High Pre-School, we believe that the first five years of a girl’s life build the foundations for her future learning, health and happiness.
Set in the extensive grounds of our Prep School in the heart of Southsea, Portsmouth, our Pre-School is based in a light and modern building with access to a large wooded garden. This is a real oasis in an inner city environment, offering plenty of space for play and exploration.
Our Early Years staff are highly qualified and quickly get to know and understand each of the children in their care. The early years are a time of incredible development, with 90% of a child’s brain development happening by age 5 (UNICEF, 2020), and our pre-school offers an outstanding start for girls from the term of their third birthday (rising 3) until they join the Reception Class.
You are warmly invited to visit us, meet Early Years teaching staff, and find out more about the opportunities available. Do Request a Prospectus and book a personal tour of the school. We are very much looking forward to meeting you and your daughter.
Ruth Irvine-Capel Head, Portsmouth High Prep and Pre-School
Children in the early years are provided with a well-planned curriculum, adept teaching and a well-resourced learning environment. As a result of these things, children settle quickly, develop confidence and learn effectively. ISI REPORT, 2026
The Power of an Early Years Education at Portsmouth High School GDST
Assistant Head and Head of Early Years, Mrs Victoria Fabre De La Grange, talks about her ethos for early learning.
The Early Years is when you have the best chance of capturing a child’s curiosity, interest and imagination and to fire their passion for learning. At Portsmouth High School, Early Years specialists ensure your daughter gets off to best possible start. Watch her grow, develop…and change.
Regular one-to-one support helping children blossom
We pride ourselves on the individual attention that each and every child receives.
Unique explorer approach to learning
We encourage children to be active explorers, not just passive recipients.
Specialist teaching
From French to music, the children have a host of additional opportunities provided by specialist teachers.
Outdoor learning in beautiful grounds
Our gardens are a hidden gem that are just waiting to be explored.

PERFORMING ARTS
MUSIC
Music is there for all, whether or not they take instrumental lessons. All music lessons involve elements of performance, composition and appraisal, with pupils working both collaboratively and individually.
Most pupils take, or have taken, private voice or instrumental lessons, and there are opportunities to perform almost every week – from informal recitals in our atrium, to large concerts in the main hall and high-profile events externally.
Our Gala Concert
Every year, we commission a new large-scale work from a renowned composer, which is performed at our Gala Concert. Most recently, we have performed Bruno Newman’s The Willow Tree, and Toby Hession’s Seasons and What Will the Children Remember? We also regularly stage full-scale musical productions, which have recently included Beauty and the Beast, Sister Act, We Will Rock You and Les Miserables.
Music beyond school...
Beyond school, we organise overseas music tours, collaborations, which range from Chichester University’s Gala Concert, to The Drifters and Foreigner’s UK concert tours, and theatre excursions for each year group (London, Glyndebourne, Bournemouth).
DRAMA
To be able to freely use her imagination, have the confidence to share her ideas and to physically show her work to others. These are our aims for your daughter’s development in drama. Because drama changes a person’s way of thinking, freeing them to approach tasks with a fresh, uninhibited energy.
In addition to the performance itself, we introduce an understanding of how plays are created and staged, along with practical design skills in costume design, set design, lighting and sound.
Drama in the curricululum
Drama is built into the curriculum from Years 7 to 9, and from Year 10, we follow AQA GCSE, enabling pupils to explore a wide range of drama, and begin to develop their own deeper understanding in their chosen areas. At A Level, academic study leads to realisation of theatre and drama, whether the practical performance or the writing about performance, and also design or directing.
CO-CURRICULAR
Run by sixth formers, our co-curricular drama clubs are very popular with girls in Years 7, 8 and 9. Girls are encouraged to direct and write their own plays, and we put on a musical every other year, with several productions happening every school year.

THE SIXTH FORM DIFFERENCE
Welcome to Portsmouth High Sixth Form
Become part of our Sixth Form...
THE FUTURE IS YOURS
Our sixth form offers a wide range of A Level subjects, with a personalised timetable created for each and every one of our pupils. So, in addition to deeper dives into subjects you already love, you can choose to pursue new subjects, and make use of the Extended Project Qualification (EPQ) to research an area of particular interest – and enhance your university applications.
Outside the classroom, we are looking to you to become a leader. And we offer a multitude of leadership initiatives to help you in this – from standing for election to the Head Girl or House Captain teams, offering peer support to your fellow pupils, representing the school in public speaking or as a member of one of our Duke of Edinburgh expedition teams, or lead a charity fundraising project… the list is endless.
You will also be coached in essential life skills in readiness for your life after school. From career guidance to money matters, cooking and driving, how to ‘wow’ at interviews and deliver the perfect presentation, we’ve got you covered.
In short, we are here to give you the confidence and competencies you need to achieve everything you want to in life.
Mrs Katie Wood Assistant Head (Pupils) and Head of Sixth Form
Pupils… engage fully in the comprehensive careers advice and economic education so that they are well prepared for the next stage of their education, training and employment. ISI REPORT, 2026

APPLY FOR NURSERY, PRE-SCHOOL & PREP
Nursery and Pre-School (ages 3-4)
Before you apply, we would encourage you to come and see us at one of our Open Events or Book a Family Visit. You will have an opportunity to see the Nursery and Pre-School, as well as the wider Prep School, learn more about our academic ethos and leading co-curricular programme, and speak with members of staff.
When you are ready, register (application) for a place. There is no registration fee for Pre-School/Nursery. We are happy to accept your application at any time.
When we have received your application, your daughter will be invited for a one-to-one settle session (morning). Our light touch approach will help your daughter to familiarise herself with the teaching team.
Before your daughter starts at Portsmouth High School, Pre School/Nursery the Head of Pre-School will speak to you further regarding the transition.

Prep School (ages 4-11)
Before you apply, we would encourage you to come and see us at one of our Open Events or Book a Family Visit at any time. You will have an opportunity to see the school, learn more about our academic ethos and leading co-curricular programme, and speak with members of staff.
When you are ready, register (application) for a place. A non-refundable fee of £60 is charged to process each child’s application. This fee is inclusive of VAT. We are happy to accept your application at any time.
Once you have registered, your daughter will be invited to attend a low-key, fun Experience Day with her current year group. We understand your daughter may be nervous ahead of her Experience Day, and we do everything to ensure her day goes smoothly. We do not have a formal assessment for the Prep School; however, in addition to the Experience Day we will request from you, your daughter’s latest school report.
At the end of her day, you will meet with the Prep School Headmaster who will share feedback on her day and next steps.

Frequently Asked Questions
Our Pre-School is split into two groups to give children the best experience possible. The Nursery Class is for the younger children, joining in the term of their third birthday. Our Pre-School is for older children preparing for Reception. With two classrooms full of exciting activities, we make sure every child is learning at their own pace, in a way that’s right for them.
At our Nursery and Pre-School, your children will learn through play. With a qualified teacher to enhance academic learning, the girls will investigate new concepts in a fun way, promoting independence, curiosity, creativity, and problem solving. Indoor and outdoor activities give girls multi-sensory first-hand experiences that make learning fun and exciting. In addition to this, the girls enjoy weekly specialist teaching for music, ballet, Outdoor learning and French classes, alongside a library session.
Portsmouth High Pre-School is a registered provider of free childcare for working parents which provides your daughter with up to 30 hours of free education a week.
Funding is available from your child’s third birthday and lasts up until the end of the term of her fifth birthday.
Our Nursery and Pre-School are open throughout the school term from 8.30 am to 3.30 pm. Morning sessions run from 8.30 am to 11.30 am and afternoons from 12.30 pm to 3.30 pm.
For the latest information on fees, please visit our dedicated fees page here.
Term dates can be found here.
Portsmouth High Prep School offers a comprehensive programme of free wraparound care for children attending full-time. Girls can join our Early Birds’ Breakfast Club from 7.30am to 8.30am and our Aftercare Club from 3.30pm to 6.00pm. For children attending part-time, wraparound care is charged at very reasonable rates.
A structured programme of care is offered through our external provider, CSS Activities, who run a holiday club at Portsmouth High Prep School during every school holiday.
There is no registration fee but there is a deposit of £60 which is refundable when your child leaves the school.
Children can start during the term of their third birthday. There are three terms during the school year starting in September. The autumn term runs from September and finishes at Christmas, the spring term runs from January until Easter and the summer term starts after Easter and ends in mid-July.

Favourite Nursery Rhymes bring Pre-School’s Sports Day to life
Our Pre-School children enjoyed their very own nursery rhyme-themed Sports Day in the beautiful grounds of the Prep School.
This year’s nursery rhyme theme brought an extra layer of fun, with races inspired by well-known favourites such as Wee Willie Winkie and Humpty Dumpty. The children delighted in showcasing the physical skills they have been developing, including skipping, balancing and running.
They performed brilliantly in front of an enthusiastic audience of parents and friends, demonstrating both confidence and teamwork.
At the end of the event, Portsmouth High Prep School’s Headmaster, Mr Marshallsay, presented the children with their well-earned medals and certificates. The afternoon concluded with a delicious tea enjoyed together in the gardens.
Nursery teacher Mrs Nelson said:
“I am so proud of all the children. They have worked hard preparing for their Sports Day and performed so well in front of an audience. Their physical skills are developing brilliantly and they will continue to build on these as they move into Reception Class.”

HOURS AND FEES
A full package of care for busy and working parents
Free childcare for working parents (Early Education Funding)
Portsmouth High Pre-School is a registered provider of free childcare for working parents which provides your daughter with up to 30 hours of free education a week.
Funding is available from your child’s third birthday and lasts up until the end of the term of her fifth birthday.
Free childcare for working parents (Early Education Funding)
The Nursery and Pre-School are open throughout the school term from 8.30am to 3.30pm. Morning sessions run from 8.30am to 11.30am and afternoons from 12.30pm to 3.30pm.
Fees for Portsmouth High Nursery and Pre-School can be found on our dedicated fees page via the link below.
Free Wraparound Care
We understand parents often need extra care for their daughters outside of the normal school day. Knowing children can safely stay on at school offers peace of mind for parents with busy schedules.
Free Wraparound Care
Free wrapround care before and after the Nursery and Pre-School day assists busy and working parents with child care on a daily basis giving peace of mind
Before and After-School care is available for all pupils from Nursery and Pre-School to Year 6 during term time.
There is no extra charge for this for pupils attending full-time. Wraparound Care is also available at very reasonable rates for Nursery and Pre-School children attending part-time.
Girls can enjoy Early Birds’ Breakfast Club from 7.30am, and choose from a varied breakfast menu for a healthy start to the day. The Aftercare Club runs from 3.30pm to 6.00pm, and offers a range of activities for younger children, or the chance to do homework, for the older girls.
Portsmouth High Prep School provides care for children during all school holidays. This means that, with school terms, provision is available for 50 weeks of the year. Holiday care is provided by CSS Activities who offer a varied range of activities to keep children happy and entertained. All holiday clubs are based on site at Portsmouth High Prep School. Please visit the CSS website for more information and costs.

MORE INFORMATION

LEARNING WITHOUT LIMITS
Being curious and learning without limits
Children are born curious and their natural curiosity is essential for developing problem solving skills, creativity and critical thinking.
The Early Years’ team at Portsmouth High School embrace the concept of learning without limits and create stimulating and supportive learning environments that encourage exploration and questioning.
Team building and collaboration
The value of working together is encouraged and actively promoted throughout Early Years.
Fostering collaboration is essential for nurturing both social and cognitive development and through modelling collaborative behaviour in discussions and demonstrating listening to one another, pupils are encouraged to build positive relationships, whilst developing empathy and learning how to appreciate diversity from an early age.
Leaders in the early years are skilled and knowledgeable and have a comprehensive understanding of the needs of individual children. ISI REPORT, 2026
Becoming independent
Becoming independent in Early Years is a pivotal part of any child’s development.
Staff support pupils to master their self-help skills nurturing their sense of autonomy and reinforces problem solving abilities. The safe and structured environment encourages exploration and decision making.
Success is celebrated and increasing responsibilities builds resilience and the self belief that they are capable of overcoming obstacles.
Building resilience
Our supportive environment allows our pupils to take risks in learning and build up resilience whilst keeping a healthy perspective on things that really matter.
This balanced approach gives them the ability to navigate challenges and sets a solid foundation for lifelong personal and academic growth.
Staff teach children phonics adeptly, ensuring that children get off to a good start in their early reading and letter formation. ISI REPORT, 2026
Being imaginative
The wonder of imagination fuels creativity, language skills and problem solving.
‘What if’ thinking, imaginative play and storytelling is encouraged and through our offering of art, music, drama and open-ended play opportunities, where there are no set rules or expectations, we are able to broaden our pupils perspectives and encourage flexible thinking. There are no limits on learning possibilities.
Wonder of learning
Every child’s learning journey is unique and our team’s understanding of every one of our pupils ensures their educational journey is tailored to their individual needs to allow them to explore their world around them.
The wonder of learning lies in being able to weave different threads of knowledge into a map of understanding. As Early Years pupils begin to make links they experience a spark of discovery that allows them to understand new concepts and change them into new ideas and our team at PHS are at hand to make sure they achieve their goals.

CURRICULUM
Introducing our curriculum
A Portsmouth High School education gives girls intellectual skills that go beyond each academic discipline so that they can use their knowledge in new situations, see connections, and problem-solve independently. It supports them individually, and keeps their personal development and wellbeing firmly at the forefront of all they do. This is what creates the scaffold that they can build their future dreams on.
'The literacy curriculum is rich, well structured and ambitious.'
YEARS 7-9
At this stage, the curriculum is based largely around subject specialisms, maintaining the collaborative enquiry-based approach developed in the prep school.
The emphasis in science is on thinking like a scientist, before learning the benefits that a more specialist disciplinary focus provides. We cover all three natural sciences, and from Year 9, biology, chemistry and physics are taught separately as IGCSE courses commence.
Girls entering Year 7 have the choice of Spanish or French as their chosen foreign language. They may continue with Latin as their second language.
CROSS CURRICULAR LEARNING
We are committed to cross-curricular learning in literacy, communication and literacy. ICT and thinking skills are taught discretely at first, but become increasingly embedded across the curriculum. Computer science is taught as a distinct strand.
CROSS CURRICULAR LEARNING
The creative arts and sport are fundamental in every child’s development. We therefore have a tailored and enhanced PSHEE (personal, social, health and economic education) programme which encourages girls to develop emotional resilience and mindfulness.

YEARS 10 TO 11
A personalised programme
At this stage, pupils build a personalised programme that creates the right balance and breadth for them. This will be created on a firm academic base, with IGCSE choices where appropriate, to ensure that the right foundations are in place for A Levels and beyond.
A personalised programme
The standard offer is nine or ten (I)GCSE subjects which must include mathematics, English language, English literature, a modern language, science(s) plus three further options. These options include Spanish, French, computer science, music, drama, Latin, religious studies, geography, history, business, classics, art and PE.
Whole-year lectures cover life skills and personal and professional development, which incorporates PSHEE. PE is on the timetable for all pupils in Years 10 and 11.
Pupils with SEND typically access the curriculum effectively and learn well. ISI REPORT, 2026
